You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image render its visual content as a pencil drawing overall?
node.criteria: Pass if the image as a whole is recognizably rendered in a pencil-drawing style, with pencil-like marks shaping the depicted content; some retained photographic detail or residual color does not by itself prevent a pass. Fail if it remains predominantly photographic or otherwise does not read overall as a pencil drawing, even if it is desaturated or has isolated sketch-like texture. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the overall style cannot be determined.
node.binding: Judge the overall rendering against the requested pencil-drawing outcome while checking that the visual content remains represented. Do not require complete removal of photographic detail or color, and do not treat isolated texture alone as sufficient.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image retains the depicted meal and table setting, while the overall scene has muted, grainy pencil-like shading and drawn contours. It reads as a pencil drawing despite some residual color and photographic detail.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is truncated and too vague to encode the full requested transformation. More importantly, its completion rule treats s1’s broad “overall reads as pencil drawing” judgment as sufficient, even though the trace describes substantial residual color and photographic detail; that endpoint-only rule collapses partial progress into yes and conflicts with the reference partial. Refine the typed criteria to distinguish visible stylistic progress from complete fulfillment, using the requested transformation and image evidence rather than accepting s1’s pass as conclusive. Ensure the partial-progress check can be evaluated when completion is uncertain, and make its dependency/activation routing explicit so a skipped s2 is not mistaken for negative evidence or silently bypassed when needed. The skipped s2 is a conditional-skip transport/coverage fact, not evidence against the edit; the concern is the semantic sufficiency threshold and routing, not that the image shows no progress. Preserve uncertainty when evidence cannot resolve completion, and do not hard-code the reference label as ground truth.
